note: [SD §1.3] makes [SD §4.7.1] the COMPLETE declaration: every type in the published record vocabulary declares its canonical subject family, its qualifier shape, and what belongs in context[]. A type with no row here, or a row with no type, is a defect and the loader refuses it. The authority column is [A8]'s, quoted and not re-derived ([SD §4.7] note 3), which is why an assigned row links to an authority-table row instead of restating its standings.
metaRecordNote: The two meta-record types (FactResolved, Correction) deliberately have no row. [SD §4.7.1] declares none, and their subject rule is fixed elsewhere: [SD §1.3] item 4 — 'on a meta-record, type names the record class and the fact key is carried explicitly… the envelope subject MUST equal the subject of the fact being resolved or corrected.' Minting rows for them here would be a declaration [SD §4.7] never made.
scoringNote: No row is marked scoreable-high. [A8 §10]'s last row lifts the bar to MEDIUM and only for the ten fact classes in [A8 §5]; [SD §4.7] note 3 bars a provisional reading from scoring a dependent decision above medium outright. So the only two values are 'capped-medium' and 'do-not-score'.

families.note: [SD §4.7] note 2: 'a family is a named, closed set of aggregate kinds — usually a singleton.' Three are not singletons and each is argued where it is declared. Every member must be a member of the aggregate enum ([SD §1.2]); the loader checks member-by-member and then checks the whole table against SUBJECT_FAMILIES in src/vocabulary.ts, because two spellings of one closed set that can drift are not one closed set.
families.anyAggregateSpellingNote: [SD §4.7] describes identity's family as 'the whole aggregate enum' without naming it. 'anyAggregate' is src/vocabulary.ts's spelling, repeated here so the family column stays a single named key. The membership is quoted; only the name is chosen.

rows.contextNote: document is the instrument the value appears on (the BL, the weight ticket); partyRole is the counterparty echoing it back. [A6 §3.2] rule D-ID: this column describes the CARRIED_SUBJECT shape — an identifier the document merely carries, asserted about that identifier's own subject. The other shape is not a context question at all: an identifier assigned to the document as an accountable artefact is asserted with the DOCUMENT as `subject`, which the declared family `anyAggregate` already admits ([SD §7.1] 'subject may be ANY aggregate kind'), and the shipment then rides in this column. The discriminator is whether the scheme is one the issuer controls for the FORM: src:cfr-49-375 §375.505(b)(16) makes 'any identification or registration number you assign to the shipment' a required BL field distinct from the BL's own number, and §375.519(a)(6) offers 'the carrier's shipment registration OR bill of lading number' as alternatives; src:dtr-part-iv A-413 §C.2 accounts for BL numbers as stock assigned to the form. Whether a given scheme is document-accountable is `identityScheme`, owed to A9, so D-ID takes it as an input.
